title: Picnic band lineup, clarinetists and records that shaped him
summary: Picnic bands ran about six pieces with banjo and no piano. He admired Lorenzo Tio and Pico; people say he plays like George Lewis.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: How many pieces would the bands have? Only six… It wouldn't be but six…

About six. That's all they used to do. I guess they used a banjo, huh? Used to use a banjo. They never used no piano in an old Dixie Ladd band. You're never singing that. What about you? Always a banjo. Guitar ever? Would they ever have a guitar player? Ghetto? Not that I remember. Let me check a little of this. See, I was wondering about some of the clarinet players that you admired out there. Well, I admired Big I, Lou, and Lorenzo Tio. I used to admire Pico, too. Well, do you think you'd play anything like those fellas that you admired at that time? I don't know. I couldn't answer that. Do you think anybody influence your style that you play today? A lot of people tell me that George Lewis and I play as pretty much alike. I don't know. I think that is about the closest one. Some of your licks are the same I've noticed, you know. But did you ever hear George in those days? When you were all? No. Well, you heard the same people, so it figures your ideas should be alike, you know. I mean, without ever thinking about it, if you listen to the same people, the ideas are going to be the same. Did you ever try to copy anybody's style in particular? No. What about listening to records? Did you ever listen to records in those times when you were young? I used to listen to records before I started playing, before I started playing.
Who were some of the people that you liked to listen to on records?
I used to like the Bruce singers, I used to like, I used to like Bruce singers like Ava Walsh, Mamie Smith.
Did you like the Karnath players on those records? Oh yeah. Jim Noon.
I haven't heard much of Jim Noon, but Johnny Dodds. You liked this playing, huh? I admired this style.
